summary: IN-M1 is fixed. isEdge now names Edge from the CHROME_BIN text as written and again from the path resolved by filepath.Abs, which is GetFullPathName on Windows, and either one refuses it. Browser still returns the CHROME_BIN text unchanged. The review's test is committed as internal/testutil/headless/edge_dot_segments_test.go, and its engine command passes. I closed the class with a corpus in testdata/chrome_bin_spellings.json, run by chrome_bin_corpus_test.go. It has 12 Edge rows that run everywhere, 10 Windows-only Edge rows (dot segments, down-and-back-up, a space before the separator, a trailing dot or space), 9 Chrome rows that must come back unchanged, and 4 non-file rows. Against HEAD's headless.go via -overlay, 10 corpus rows and all 5 review-test subtests failed. With the fix, everything passes, as does the full suite with CHROME_BIN unset and set.

files.why: isEdge checks the raw CHROME_BIN text and the filepath.Abs-resolved path (new namesEdge helper does the base-name test); comment explains why
the code review's TestBrowserRefusesEdgeBehindDotSegments, as given (five dot-segment spellings of msedge.exe must skip naming CHROME_BIN)
the corpus of CHROME_BIN spellings whose last text element is not the file the OS opens: edge, chrome and skip rows, with windows_only flags

TestChromeBinSpellingsCorpus expands each corpus row against a temp folder holding empty msedge.exe, chrome.exe, Edge/Application/chrome.exe and sub/, and asserts the Browser outcome (nothing is started)

obligations.how: In isEdge I added filepath.Abs resolution next to the raw-text check, via a namesEdge helper, so msedge.exe\., \.\., \x\.., /., 'msedge.exe \.', a trailing dot and a trailing space are all refused with a skip that says Microsoft Edge and names CHROME_BIN. The returned path is still the CHROME_BIN text. The review's test is in place as edge_dot_segments_test.go and `go test -count=1 -run TestBrowserRefusesEdgeBehindDotSegments ./internal/testutil/headless/` passes. The corpus's quiet rows (Chrome with the same dot segments, a Chrome inside folders called Edge, folders, a missing file) guard against a rule that refuses everything. Before the fix (HEAD's headless.go through -overlay): 10 corpus rows and 5 of 5 review-test subtests failed. Mutation: making the Abs branch return namesEdge(abs) && false fails the review's test.

not_built: O-003 / m1 (the recorder's doc comment in default_browser_test.go still mentions Fatalf): a person waived it as note N-223, a comment-only fix left to the comment fixer, so I did not touch it.
follow_ups: Symlinks or hard links named chrome.exe that point at msedge.exe are not caught, because the check is by name and not by resolving links. That is not an ordinary-input spelling, so the corpus does not claim it. If it matters, resolving the target with filepath.EvalSymlinks in isEdge would close it.

tests.note: Expected: 10 corpus rows (the dot-segment, down-and-back-up and space-before-separator Edge spellings) and all 5 review-test subtests failed.
